title: Elastic Load Balancing
description: Learn about Application, Network, and Gateway Load Balancers and how to distribute traffic across your applications.

data.text: Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) automatically distributes incoming traffic across multiple targets — such as EC2 instances, containers, and IP addresses — in multiple Availability Zones. This increases the availability and fault tolerance of your application.
AWS offers three different load balancers, each optimized for a specific use case.

cards.title: Application Load Balancer (ALB)
cards.description: Best for HTTP and HTTPS traffic at the application layer (OSI Layer 7).

cards.title: Network Load Balancer (NLB)
cards.description: Best for extreme performance and static IP needs at the transport layer (OSI Layer 4).
cons: More complex to configure than ALB

cards.title: Gateway Load Balancer (GLB)
cards.description: Best for deploying and scaling third-party virtual appliances (firewalls, IDS/IPS).
pros: Combines load balancing with transparent network gateways

data.text: Target groups route requests to registered targets such as EC2 instances, IP addresses, or Lambda functions. Health checks monitor the health of registered targets and only route traffic to healthy ones.

data.title: Health Check Settings
items: **Protocol** — HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, or TLS depending on the load balancer type
**Timeout** — how long to wait for a response
**Healthy threshold** — number of consecutive successes to mark healthy
**Unhealthy threshold** — number of consecutive failures to mark unhealthy

data.text: Stickiness (session affinity) ensures that requests from the same client are always sent to the same target. You can enable stickiness at the target group level. For HTTPS traffic, you can offload SSL/TLS decryption at the load balancer using an SSL certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).

data.title: Create a Target Group and Listener with AWS CLI
data.content: This command creates an ALB target group and adds a listener rule.
data.code:
# Create target group for HTTP traffic
aws elbv2 create-target-group \
  --name my-app-targets \
  --protocol HTTP \
  --port 80 \
  --vpc-id vpc-0123456789abcdef0 \
  --health-check-path /health \
  --health-check-interval-seconds 30

# Register EC2 instances with the target group
aws elbv2 register-targets \
  --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456789012:targetgroup/my-app-targets/abcdef123456 \
  --targets Id=i-0123456789abcdef0 Id=i-0abcdef1234567890

# Create listener on the ALB
aws elbv2 create-listener \
  --load-balancer-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456789012:loadbalancer/app/my-alb/abcdef123456 \
  --protocol HTTP \
  --port 80 \
  --default-actions Type=forward,TargetGroupArn=arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456789012:targetgroup/my-app-targets/abcdef123456

terms.definition: A logical group of targets (EC2 instances, IPs, Lambda functions) that a load balancer routes traffic to.
A periodic check that determines whether a target is healthy and should receive traffic.
Decrypting HTTPS traffic at the load balancer so backend servers receive unencrypted HTTP traffic.

data.title: Configure an Application Load Balancer
data.description: Create an ALB in the AWS console with two EC2 instances behind it. Set up a health check on the /health path.
steps: Launch two EC2 instances in different Availability Zones
Create a target group with HTTP health checks
Register both EC2 instances with the target group
Create a listener rule that forwards traffic to the target group
Test the ALB DNS name in your browser
data.expectedOutcome: Your ALB should successfully route traffic between both healthy instances and stop routing to any instance that fails its health check.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: ALB handles HTTP/HTTPS at Layer 7; NLB handles TCP/UDP at Layer 4
Target groups route traffic to registered targets
Health checks ensure traffic only goes to healthy targets
SSL termination at the ALB offloads encryption from your servers
data.takeaway: Load balancers are the first line of defense for availability and scalability. They let you add or remove servers without downtime.
